chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abu Jamilyah, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
In a sheep that drank wine until it became intoxicated, then was slaughtered while in that state, the contents of its stomach are not to be eaten.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the stomach contents of an animal slaughtered while intoxicated?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishing that intoxication in an animal renders its stomach contents impure or inedible, extending the concept of *khamr* (wine) beyond mere consumption to the state of the beast. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that the internal state of the animal affects the purity of its parts, specifically distinguishing the stomach contents from the rest of the carcass. It serves as a practical application of the broader principle that intoxicants carry a spiritual and physical impurity that transfers to the consumed entity.
